sentiment.rationale: The company's forward guidance was significantly reduced: full-year 2025 sales are now forecast to decline by a low double-digit percentage (previously low- to mid-single-digit increase), and EBIT is expected to be a loss (previously €445-525 million). The Q3 results show a sharp sales decline, a net loss, and management describes 2025 as a 'reset year' with 2026 as a 'transition year', indicating a prolonged downturn. The outlook is cautious and defensive, with no positive forward revision, justifying a strongly bearish sentiment.

summary.revenue: Q3 2025 sales decreased by 10.4% currency-adjusted to €1,955.7 million (reported -15.3%). 9M 2025 sales decreased by 4.3% currency-adjusted to €5,973.9 million (reported -8.5%).
summary.guidance: FY 2025 outlook confirmed: currency-adjusted sales expected to decline by a low double-digit percentage, reported EBIT loss expected, capex around €250 million. Previously (as of 24 July 2025) sales were expected to decline low double-digit percentage (previously low- to mid-single-digit increase) and EBIT was expected to be a loss (previously €445-525 million).
summary.margin: Q3 2025 gross profit margin declined by 260 bps to 45.2%. Adjusted EBIT margin was 2.0% (Q3 2024: 10.3%). Reported EBIT margin was 1.5%. 9M 2025 gross margin declined by 130 bps to 46.1%.
key_risks: Muted brand momentum and low brand heat
Low distribution quality, including high share of mass merchants
Impact of U.S. tariffs (mitigated to ~€50 million in FY 2025)
Currency headwinds (U.S. Dollar, Argentine Peso, Mexican Peso)
Cost efficiency program with additional ~900 white-collar role reductions
Potential shift of PUMA United to licensing model (uncertainty)
Negative free cash flow of €-685.8 million in 9M 2025
key_opportunities: DTC business growth: Q3 DTC +4.5% ca, e-commerce +5.6% ca, retail stores +3.9% ca
Growth in performance categories: Basketball and Performance Running delivered healthy growth
Speedcat family continued to perform extremely well in APAC
Strong momentum in Training with HYROX partnership
Strategic priorities to become Top 3 global sports brand
Expanded cost efficiency program to reduce cost base
Inventory clean-up expected to return to normalized levels by end of 2026

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management acknowledges significant challenges and describes 2025 as a 'reset year' and 2026 as a 'transition year', with cautious language about the remainder of 2025.

evidence.claim: Q3 2025 sales decreased by 10.4% currency-adjusted to €1,955.7 million.
evidence.quote: Sales decrease by 10.4% on a currency-adjusted basis (ca) to € 1,955.7 million (-15.3% reported), vastly due to strategic reset initiatives

evidence.claim: 9M 2025 sales decreased by 4.3% currency-adjusted to €5,973.9 million.
evidence.quote: sales in the first nine months of 2025 decreased by 4.3% (ca) to € 5,973.9 million with a decline across all regions and product divisions.
Consequently, net loss amounted to € -62.3 million (Q3 2024: net income of € 127.8 million) and earnings per share came in at € -0.42 (Q3 2024: € 0.86).
Consequently, net loss came in at € -308.9 million (9M 2024: net income of € 257.1 million) and earnings per share amounted to € -2.09 (9M 2024: € 1.72).

evidence.claim: FY 2025 outlook confirmed: currency-adjusted sales decline low double-digit, EBIT loss, capex ~€250 million.
evidence.quote: PUMA confirms its full-year 2025 outlook. Sales on a currency-adjusted basis are forecast to decline by a low double-digit percentage, a reported EBIT loss is expected and capital expenditures of around € 250 million.

evidence.claim: Prior guidance (as of 24 July 2025) was for a low double-digit sales decline and EBIT loss, revised from earlier expectations.
evidence.quote: Currency adjusted sales are now forecast to decline low double-digit percentage (Previously: low- to mid-single-digit percentage currency adjusted increase). ... For the EBIT we expect a loss in the full year 2025 (Previously: EBIT of € 445 million to € 525 million)

evidence.claim: Q3 2025 gross profit margin declined by 260 bps to 45.2%.
evidence.quote: The gross profit margin declined by 260 basis points to 45.2% (Q3 2024: 47.9%)

evidence.claim: Q3 2025 adjusted EBIT margin was 2.0%.
evidence.quote: ADJUSTED EBIT (% of Sales) 39.5(2.0%)

evidence.claim: Q3 2025 reported EBIT margin was 1.5%.
evidence.quote: Consequently, the reported EBIT came in at € 29.4 million (Q3 2024: € 237.0 million), resulting in a reported EBIT margin of 1.5% (Q3 2024: 10.3%).

evidence.claim: 9M 2025 gross margin declined by 130 bps to 46.1%.
evidence.quote: The gross profit margin declined by 130 basis points to 46.1% (9M 2024: 47.4%).

evidence.claim: Inventories increased by 17.3% to €2,124.1 million.
evidence.quote: Inventories increase by 17.3% to € 2,124.1 million; Inventory clean-up initiated, and PUMA expects to return to normalised levels by the end of 2026

evidence.claim: U.S. tariffs impact mitigated to around €50 million in FY 2025.
evidence.quote: MITIGATED NEGATIVE IMPACT ON GROSS PROFIT OF AROUND € 50 MILLION IN FY 2025(PREVIOUSLY: AROUND € 80 MILLION)

evidence.claim: Free cash flow was negative €-685.8 million in 9M 2025.
evidence.quote: This led to a free cashflow in the first nine months of 2025 of € -685.8 million (9M 2024: € -287.4 million).

evidence.claim: DTC business grew 4.5% ca in Q3 2025.
evidence.quote: The Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) business grew by 4.5% (ca) to € 570.0 million.

evidence.claim: Basketball and Performance Running delivered healthy growth.
evidence.quote: PUMA’s performance categories Basketball and Performance Running remained resilient and delivered healthy growth, supported by the successful launch of product innovations such as the HALI 1 basketball shoe and the Velocity NITRO ™ 4 running shoe.

evidence.claim: Speedcat family performed extremely well in APAC.
evidence.quote: This was partially offset by growth in Sportstyle Prime driven by the Speedcat family, which continued to perform extremely well in APAC during the third quarter

evidence.claim: Training category has strong momentum with HYROX.
evidence.quote: This was partially offset by growth in Training with strong momentum in HYROX — a standout performance trend that continues to gain traction globally and where PUMA is the exclusive partner

evidence.claim: Management tone is cautious.
evidence.quote: While 2025 is a year of reset and 2026 will be a transition year, we are confident that the measures outlined above are an important first step in returning PUMA to growth from 2027 onwards.

evidence.claim: Management acknowledges muted brand momentum and low distribution quality.
evidence.quote: PUMA has to address the fact that it has become too commercial, which is reflected in muted brand heat, low distribution quality, and a product offering that is not cutting through in the market.

evidence.claim: Cost efficiency program expanded with ~900 additional role reductions.
evidence.quote: PUMA plans a targeted reduction of additional around 900 white-collar roles globally (total number: around 7,000) by the end of 2026

evidence.claim: PUMA United may shift to licensing model.
evidence.quote: As part of the ongoing reset measures and efforts to optimise the PUMA distribution network, PUMA is considering moving from a partnership model to a licensing model in 2025.

evidence.claim: Currency headwinds negatively impacted sales.
evidence.quote: Currencies, especially U.S. Dollar and Argentine Peso, had a negative impact, reducing sales in euro terms by approximately € 125 million.

evidence.claim: Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility is a risk.
evidence.quote: Amid ongoing volatile geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility, PUMA anticipates that both sector-wide and company-specific challenges will significantly impact performance for the remainder of 2025.
